name: Northrop Grumman

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Northrop Grumman logo blue-on-clear 2020.svg)

description: Northrop Grumman builds military aircraft (the B-21 Raider bomber, F-35 centre fuselage, E-2D, unmanned systems), strategic missiles (Sentinel ICBM) and munitions, radar and electronic-warfare systems, and satellites and launch systems. The US government bought 84 percent of 2025 sales. Revenue is recognised as work is done on long-term contracts, so profit hinges on cost estimates: the fixed-price B-21 low-rate production phase has lost about $2.0 billion cumulatively. Backlog was $95.7 billion at year-end 2025 and $104.7 billion at 2026-06-30.

Mowgli classification is not set here.

businessLines.name: Aeronautics Systems
businessLines.how: The US Air Force, Navy and international customers pay under cost-type and fixed-price development and production contracts; revenue is booked as costs are incurred, and the fixed-price B-21 low-rate production phase carried a loss provision.
businessLines.description: Military aircraft: B-21 Raider, F-35 centre fuselage, E-2D Advanced Hawkeye, TACAMO, unmanned systems; sustainment and modernisation.

revenue.note: Value shown is external sales (reported segment sales $12,992M minus $167M intersegment, computed). FY2024 reported $12,396M.

businessLines.name: Defense Systems
businessLines.how: The US Air Force, Army and Navy and allies pay under production and development contracts for missiles, munitions and propulsion; development programs like Sentinel are ramping while ammunition is produced in volume.
businessLines.description: Strategic deterrent (Sentinel ICBM), tactical weapons and armament including military ammunition, missile defense solutions.

businessLines.name: Mission Systems
businessLines.how: Defense and intelligence customers pay for sensor, radar and electronics systems delivered under production contracts, plus sustainment; a large share of its sales goes to other Northrop segments (platforms), hence $1.4B of intersegment sales.
businessLines.description: Radar (airborne and ground-based), electro-optical/infrared sensors, electronic warfare, navigation, command and control, marine systems, networked communications.

businessLines.how: Government customers pay under cost-reimbursable and fixed-price development and production contracts for satellites, launch and propulsion; 2025 sales fell 8% as restricted space and NGI programs wound down.
businessLines.description: Space, missile defense and launch systems for national security, civil government and commercial customers: satellites, launch vehicles and solid rocket motors, Next Generation Interceptor, restricted programs.
